Hi all — quick guidance from Finance/Tax:

- Redwood does not currently hold an Indian GSTIN. For cross-border B2B supply of cloud/saas/inference services, Indian tax law generally requires the recipient (registered in India) to self-assess IGST under the reverse-charge mechanism (RCM) where the supplier is located outside India.

- Practical implications for invoicing: Redwood should issue a tax invoice showing the service value and a clear note such as: "Reverse charge: Recipient to self-assess and pay IGST under Section 5(3) (import of services)." Do NOT add Indian GST amounts on the supplier invoice if Redwood has no GSTIN.

- Required invoice data to help VidyaApps process and reclaim (if applicable):
  * Supplier legal name and address (Redwood Inference, US address)
  * Supplier tax id (US EIN)
  * Customer (recipient) legal name and Indian GSTIN (15 characters)
  * Invoice value in USD or agreed currency and exchange rate (if they need INR value)
  * Statement of reverse-charge / recipient liability wording
  * PO number and any AP reference

- Action items for VidyaApps: please confirm your GSTIN (we will validate format), AP email for sending invoice, and whether you need us to include an INR equivalent.

I attached a short checklist we use for GST validation & invoice formatting.

Karthik
Finance, Redwood Inference
